chunks: Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Ammār narrated from Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man comes to me seeking to buy silk from me, while I do not have any of it. So he negotiates with me, and I negotiate with him regarding the profit and the term, until we come to an agreement on something. Then I go and buy it for him and call him to it.

So he said: Tell me, if he finds a sale that is more preferable to him than what is with you, is he able to turn away to it and leave you? Or if you find that, are you able to turn away from him and leave him?
I said: Yes. He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.الرِّبْحِ: profit margin agreed upon in the proposed sale
key_terms.الْأَجَلِ: the deferred term or payment deadline
key_terms.الْحَرِيرِ: silk, the commodity being discussed in the transaction
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Islam to negotiate a sale before owning the item, then buy it and sell it afterward?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a commercial arrangement in which a seller first negotiates with a buyer, then goes to acquire the goods afterward. Imam Abū 'Abdillāh عليه السلام permits this so long as neither party is bound before the item is actually obtained and each remains free to withdraw. It relates to financial law and the avoidance of impermissible binding sales before ownership or possession.
